posts.seoTitle: North Dakota Speeding Ticket: Fine and Points
posts.description: $3 per mph over ($5 where the limit is above 65), $20 minimum. Up to 10 over is 0 points. You have 14 days to pay, contest or elect a course.
posts.answer: North Dakota charges $3 per mph over, $20 minimum, or $5 per mph where the limit is above 65, plus $20 at 16 over. School zones start at $40 and work zones at $150. Up to 10 over is 0 points where the limit is 65 or less. Within 14 days, pay, request a hearing, or elect a course in writing when you post bond.

keyFacts.label: First points
keyFacts.value: 11 over (6 over where the limit is above 65)

faq.q: How much is 20 over on a road posted above 65 in North Dakota?
faq.a: $120. That's $5 for each of the 20 miles per hour, plus the $20 added at 16 over, under NDCC 39-06.1-06(6). It's also 5 points.

faq.q: Does 11 over put points on my North Dakota license?
faq.a: Yes. Where the limit is 65 or less, 11 to 15 over is 1 point. Where the limit is above 65, it's 3 points.

faq.q: Can I pay my speeding ticket online and still take the course instead of points?
faq.a: No. The state courts' payment page says "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT" if you have questions about taking a defensive driving course. The election goes to the clerk in writing with your bond, by mail or in person.

faq.q: Can one speeding ticket suspend my license in North Dakota?
faq.a: Yes. 36 over where the limit is 65 or less, or 31 over where it's above 65, is 12 points by itself. Twelve points is a 7-day suspension.

faq.q: Is it worth electing the course for a 1-point speeding ticket?
faq.a: Usually not. One point comes off by itself after three months with no new points. The election also uses up your once-a-year chance and gives up the 3-point reduction option.

posts.content:
## What does a speeding ticket cost in North Dakota?

$3 for each mile per hour over the limit, or $20, whichever is more. Where the limit is posted above 65, it's $5 per mile per hour with the same $20 floor. At 16 over or more, another $20 is added. That's [NDCC 39-06.1-06](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf), subsections 4 and 6.

| Mph over | Limit 65 or less | Limit above 65 |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | $20 | $25 |
| 10 | $30 | $50 |
| 11 | $33 | $55 |
| 15 | $45 | $75 |
| 16 | $68 | $100 |
| 20 | $80 | $120 |
| 25 | $95 | $145 |
| 30 | $110 | $170 |
| 35 | $125 | $195 |

We calculated these from the statute. The amount printed on your citation is the one you owe.

School zones and work zones have their own floor. In a school zone it's $40 for 1 to 10 over, then $1 for each mph past 10. In a work zone it's $150 for 1 to 10 over, then $2 for each mph past 10, but only when workers are present and the sign says "Minimum Fee $150." If the regular fee works out higher, the regular fee applies. [School zone and work zone tickets](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-school-zone-work-zone-speeding) has the details, and [what a speeding ticket costs](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-cost) has more worked numbers.

## How many points is a speeding ticket?

Zero to 15, depending on how fast and on the posted limit. The two schedules are in [NDCC 39-06.1-10](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf), subsection 3(a), paragraphs 30 and 33.

| Mph over | Limit 65 or less | Limit above 65 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 to 5 | 0 | 0 |
| 6 to 10 | 0 | 1 |
| 11 to 15 | 1 | 3 |
| 16 to 20 | 3 | 5 |
| 21 to 25 | 5 | 7 |
| 26 to 30 | 9 | 10 |
| 31 to 35 | 9 | 12 |
| 36 to 45 | 12 | 15 |
| 46 or more | 15 | 15 |

School and work zone tickets use the same points. The bigger fee doesn't add any. NDDOT suspends at 12, so 36 over on a road posted 65 or less is a suspension on its own. [Speeding ticket points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-points) goes through each band, and [North Dakota speed limits](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speed-limits) tells you which table your road falls under.

## What should I do in the first 14 days?

Pick one of these before the 14 days from the citation date run out:

1. Pay the fee or post bond. That admits the violation, the court reports it, and NDDOT enters the points.
2. Ask for a hearing. You sign the request on the citation and post a bond equal to the fee. [How the hearing works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-traffic-ticket-hearing).
3. Elect a driver training course in lieu of points. You still post the bond, and you tell the clerk in writing at the same time.

Option 3 is where people trip. The state courts' payment page says: "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT if you are requesting a hearing for a traffic case" or have questions about taking a defensive driving course ([ndcourts.gov](https://www.ndcourts.gov/public-access)). The court's own self-help guide says you notify the clerk by mailing written notice in the same envelope as the citation, or handing it over when you pay in person ([ND Legal Self Help Center](https://www.ndcourts.gov/Media/Default/Legal%20Resources/Legal%20Self%20Help/Other%20Forms/Administrative-Traffic-Elect-Driving-Course.pdf)). There is no online way to elect. [Should I pay my ticket?](/north-dakota/blog/should-i-pay-my-north-dakota-ticket) walks through the choice.

## Which speeding tickets can I keep off my record?

Any worth 5 points or fewer. That's up to 25 over where the limit is 65 or less, and up to 20 over where it's above 65. [NDCC 39-06.1-10.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf) sets the rest:

- once in 12 months, counted back from the date on the new ticket
- NDDOT needs your certificate within 30 days of telling the clerk
- the bond is forfeited anyway, so the fee doesn't go down
- electing "forfeits any point reduction option under section 39-06.1-13," which is the 3-point reduction

The steps are in [how to elect the course at court](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election). Our course is 4 hours online, $24.99 with the certificate, and it's [on the course page](/north-dakota).

## Who shouldn't buy a course for this ticket?

Anyone whose ticket is 0 points. That's up to 10 over where the limit is 65 or less and up to 5 over where it's higher. There's nothing to keep off.

A 1-point ticket is close to the same answer. NDDOT removes a point for every three months without new points ([NDCC 39-06.1-13(1)](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)), so it's gone in a season. Spending your once-a-year election and the 3-point option on it is a bad trade.

The exceptions are drivers near a limit. If you're at 11 points, one more suspends you. If you're under 18, the license is canceled at 6 points ([NDCC 39-06-01.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06.pdf)), so a 1-point ticket at 5 points matters.

## What about racing or showing off?

Those aren't speeding tickets. Exhibition driving is 3 points. Racing is 10, which can't be elected away. [Exhibition driving and racing tickets](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-exhibition-driving-racing-ticket).

## Speeding guides

- [Fee by speed](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-cost)

- [Electing a course in lieu of points](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election)

posts.seoTitle: North Dakota Traffic Ticket: What to Do Next
posts.description: You have 14 days to pay, ask for a hearing or elect a course in lieu of points. Which court has your ticket, the points, and what ignoring it costs.
posts.answer: You have 14 days from the date on the citation. Paying admits the violation and the points go on your record. Asking for a hearing makes the state prove it. For a ticket worth 5 points or fewer, you can elect a driver training course in writing when you post bond, which keeps the points off. Don't pay online if you want the course.

keyFacts.label: Course in lieu of points
keyFacts.value: Tickets worth 5 points or fewer, once in 12 months

keyFacts.label: Certificate due
keyFacts.value: 30 days after you tell the clerk

faq.q: Is a North Dakota traffic ticket a criminal charge?
faq.a: Most aren't. NDCC 39-06.1-10 splits the point schedule into noncriminal and criminal violations, and speeding, stop signs and failing to yield are noncriminal. Reckless driving, leaving the scene and fleeing an officer are on the criminal list.

faq.q: Do I have to go to court for a traffic ticket in North Dakota?
faq.a: Not for a noncriminal ticket, unless you ask for a hearing. You can pay or post bond by mail or at the clerk's window within 14 days. The offenses listed in NDCC 39-06.1-05, such as reckless driving and driving under suspension, can't be handled that way.

faq.q: Which court handles a Highway Patrol ticket in North Dakota?
faq.a: The district court for the county where you were stopped. City police tickets written under a city ordinance go to that city's municipal court. The court is named on your citation.

faq.q: Does a city ticket count toward my state points?
faq.a: Yes. The point schedule covers each violation "or equivalent ordinance," and NDDOT enters the points, not the city. The Bismarck court says it "has no authority regarding drivers' licenses or points."

faq.q: How many tickets does it take to lose your license in North Dakota?
faq.a: It's points, not tickets. Two 6-point tickets, such as careless driving and no insurance, reach 12 and a 7-day suspension. Six 2-point tickets do the same, unless time or a course takes points off in between.

posts.content:
## What are my choices?

Three, and you have 14 days from the date on the citation to pick one.

1. Pay the fee or post bond. That admits the violation. The court reports it to NDDOT and NDDOT enters the points.
2. Ask for a hearing. Sign the request on the citation and post a bond equal to the fee. The prosecution has to prove the violation. [How the hearing works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-traffic-ticket-hearing).
3. Elect a driver training course in lieu of points. You post the bond and tell the clerk, in writing, at the same time. The violation is admitted, but the points aren't entered if you finish the course on time.

[Should I pay my ticket?](/north-dakota/blog/should-i-pay-my-north-dakota-ticket) helps you choose.

## How does the course election work?

[NDCC 39-06.1-10.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf) sets the rules:

- the ticket has to be worth 5 points or fewer
- you can't have elected in the 12 months before the date on this ticket
- the offense can't be one listed in 39-06.1-05 (reckless driving, DUI, leaving the scene, driving under suspension and a few others)
- you notify the court "at the time of posting the bond," and the bond is forfeited anyway
- NDDOT has to receive proof of completion within 30 days after you notify the court
- electing "forfeits any point reduction option under section 39-06.1-13," which is the 3-point reduction

The court's self-help guide adds the practical part. Mail your written notice in the same envelope as the citation, or hand it to the clerk when you pay in person. And: "The Clerk of Court and the instructor of the course aren't responsible for submitting your certificate to the NDDOT. This Is Your Responsibility!" ([ND Legal Self Help Center](https://www.ndcourts.gov/Media/Default/Legal%20Resources/Legal%20Self%20Help/Other%20Forms/Administrative-Traffic-Elect-Driving-Course.pdf)). You email it to drs@nd.gov.

More: [electing the course at court](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election), [the 30-day deadline](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-in-lieu-of-points-30-day-deadline), and [which tickets qualify](/north-dakota/blog/which-tickets-qualify-in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota).

## Which court has my ticket?

The one named on the citation. A city police officer writing under a city ordinance sends it to that city's municipal court. A Highway Patrol trooper or a county deputy sends it to the district court for the county.

Most courts take payment through the state courts' site at [ndcourts.gov/public-access](https://www.ndcourts.gov/public-access). You search "State of North Dakota" or the city, by name or citation number. Visa, MasterCard and Discover only, no American Express, and the courts say to allow 4 days from the citation before it shows up ([pay fines instructions](https://www.ndcourts.gov/public-access/pay-fines)). Minot's municipal court lists no online option; it takes payment in person, by mail, by drop box or by phone at 701-857-4759.

The same payment page opens with: "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT if you are requesting a hearing for a traffic case" or have questions about taking a defensive driving course. If you want either, don't pay there. [How to pay online](/north-dakota/blog/how-to-pay-north-dakota-traffic-ticket-online).

City guides, with each court's address, phone and hours:

- [Fargo](/north-dakota/blog/fargo-traffic-ticket)
- [Bismarck](/north-dakota/blog/bismarck-traffic-ticket)
- [Grand Forks](/north-dakota/blog/grand-forks-traffic-ticket)
- [Minot](/north-dakota/blog/minot-traffic-ticket)
- [West Fargo](/north-dakota/blog/west-fargo-traffic-ticket)
- [Mandan](/north-dakota/blog/mandan-traffic-ticket)
- [Williston](/north-dakota/blog/williston-traffic-ticket)

## How many points will it put on my record?

It depends on the violation. These are from [NDCC 39-06.1-10](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf), and NDDOT publishes the same values.

| Violation | Points |
|---|---|
| Child not in a restraint or seat belt | 1 |
| Failing to dim headlights | 1 |
| Failing to yield | 2 |
| Stop sign or red light | 2 |
| Failing to use the care required | 2 |
| Exhibition driving | 3 |
| Failing to stop at a railroad crossing | 3 |
| Careless driving | 6 |
| Passing a stopped school bus | 6 |
| No liability insurance, first | 6 |
| Reckless driving | 8 |
| Racing | 10 |
| Leaving the scene, property damage | 14 |
| Fleeing a peace officer | 24 |

Speeding runs from 0 to 15. The bands are on the [speeding ticket](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket) page. Everything else is in [points by violation](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-by-violation).

Some tickets carry no points at all: speeding up to 10 over where the limit is 65 or less (up to 5 over where it's higher), driving without a license, overtime parking under a city ordinance, a seat belt ticket, and texting. NDDOT's page says it plainly: "For violations not listed, no points are assigned." Pay those. A course does nothing for them.

## When do points cost me my license?

At 12 points NDDOT suspends you for 7 days, and 7 more for each point over 12 ([NDCC 39-06.1-10(2)](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)). [License suspended for points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-license-suspended-for-points) has the table.

Under 18, the line is lower. NDCC 39-06-01.1 has the director cancel the license at a total "in excess of five points" for acts committed as a minor, and after cancellation you're treated as never having held a license ([NDCC 39-06-01.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06.pdf)). [Points for drivers under 18](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-under-18-points-license-cancellation).

Points come off by 1 every three months without new points, and by 3 when you send NDDOT a certificate from an approved course, once in 12 months ([NDCC 39-06.1-13](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)). Ours is 4 hours online for $24.99 on [the course page](/north-dakota).

## What if I ignore it?

It doesn't go away. The court's hearing guide says failing to appear at a hearing without just cause "is considered an admission of the charged traffic violation" ([ND Legal Self Help Center](https://www.ndcourts.gov/Media/Default/Legal%20Resources/Legal%20Self%20Help/Other%20Forms/Administrative%20Traffic%20Hearings.pdf)), so the points post anyway. NDDOT can also suspend your license for failing to appear or post bond, and lists a $50 reinstatement fee for that suspension ([NDDOT driver record services](https://www.dot.nd.gov/driver/driver-record-services-and-suspensions)). Call the court on your citation before the 14 days are up.

faq.q: Is the North Dakota Safety Council course the only one NDDOT accepts?
faq.a: No. NDSC is one of 21 providers on NDDOT's list. It is the only one on the list with classrooms in Bismarck, Fargo and Minot.

faq.q: Does a $5 course take off the same points as a $40 one?
faq.a: Yes. NDDOT doesn't grade courses. Any approved course takes 3 points off once every 12 months, and NDCC 39-06.1-13 caps the total at 9 points in three years.

faq.q: Why isn't Road Ready Safety on NDDOT's list?
faq.a: NDDOT approved our course on September 29, 2026, and its public web list hasn't been updated yet. The page has no date stamp, so there's no way to tell from the page when it was last changed.

faq.q: Will NDDOT accept a course that isn't approved?
faq.a: No. The reduction in NDCC 39-06.1-13 is for a course "approved by the director." A course sold as defensive driving but not approved by NDDOT won't change your points.

faq.q: Does NDDOT's list show which courses also count for insurance?
faq.a: No. NDDOT's list is for points only. The Highway Patrol keeps the insurance lists, and nine providers on NDDOT's list are not on them.

posts.content:
## Which defensive driving courses does NDDOT approve?

Twenty-one, as of October 5, 2026. NDDOT lists them under "Defensive Driving Courses" on its [points reduction page](https://www.dot.nd.gov/driver/driver-education/driver-license-points-reduction-and-points-schedule) and introduces them as "Approved online courses for up to a 3 point reduction" that "can be taken once every 12 months." The page carries no date and no phone numbers. Each provider's name is a link to its site.

Our course is NDDOT-approved and costs $24.99 for 4 hours online, but NDDOT's public list has not yet been updated to show it, so it isn't in the table below.

## All 21 courses, in NDDOT's order

Prices, hours and format are from each provider's own North Dakota page, checked October 5, 2026. "Not stated" means the page didn't give that number when we looked.

| # | Provider (as NDDOT names it) | Price | Hours | Format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0-Point Defensive Driving by Defensive Driving Institute | $18.95 | 4 to 6 | Online |
| 2 | #01-1stDrive | $19.19 | Not stated | Online |
| 3 | #1 Defensive Driving Course | $24.98 | Not stated | Online |
| 4 | 1 Stop Defensive Driving | $19.95 | Not stated | Online |
| 5 | 4 Hour Point Reduction Course by DriveSafeToday | $24.95 | 4 | Online |
| 6 | 5 Dollar Traffic School | $5 | 4, no timers | Online |
| 7 | AAA ND Roadwise Driver | Not stated | Not stated | Online |
| 8 | AARP Driver Safety Program | $27 members, $30 others | 4 | Online |
| 9 | Alive at 25 | Not stated | 4 or 4.5 | Classroom or live online |
| 10 | DriveSafe Online Defensive Driving Course | $24.95 | 4 | Online |
| 11 | Driving School of America | $19.95 | About 4 | Online |
| 12 | Driving University | $29.95 | Not stated | Online |
| 13 | NSC | $24.95 | Not stated | Online |
| 14 | National Traffic Safety Institute (Safe New Attitude Program) | $39.95 | 4 | Online |
| 15 | North Dakota Safety Council | $45 to $95 | 4 or 5 | Classroom, live online or online |
| 16 | North Dakota Driver Safety Program (Traffic Safety Consultants) | $35.00 | At least 4 | Online |
| 17 | Pass Fast With AI | $25.00 | 4 | Online |
| 18 | Safe2Drive | $27.95 | 4 | Online |
| 19 | Safe Streets Academy | $30 | 4 | Online |
| 20 | T.H.I.N.K. Defensive Driving by TrainND Northwest | Not stated | Not stated | Classroom, Williston |
| 21 | Traffic School Online | $29.97 | Not stated | Online |

A few rows need a note.

- NSC: NDDOT links NSC's home page. The $24.95 is NSC's North Dakota course sold through State Farm. Neither page says whether that is the course NDDOT means.
- AAA: the price appears only after you start the sign-up.
- Alive at 25: NDSC runs it as a 4-hour classroom course or a 4.5-hour distance learning course. NDSC's Alive at 25 page gives no price.
- National Traffic Safety Institute: its page says you need "special permission from a court, employer, or insurance company" to use its programs.
- TrainND Northwest: classroom only, in Williston. Its listing showed "No classes found" on October 5.
- North Dakota Safety Council prices depend on the course and who is paying:

| NDSC course | Member | Non-member | Court or DOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4-hour classroom | $60 | $65 | $85 |
| 4-hour live distance learning | $75 | $80 | $95 |
| 5-hour self-paced online | $49 | $59 | $80 |

## How many hours does an NDDOT course have to be?

NDDOT doesn't set a number. Its points page states no minimum, and neither does its Driver Refresher Courses page. [NDCC 39-06.1-13](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf) only requires "a driver training course approved by the director." The one hour figure on NDDOT's list is part of a provider's name.

Most providers that state a length say 4 hours. Several don't state one at all.

## Is there a 5-hour course?

Yes, one. The North Dakota Safety Council sells a 5-hour self-paced online course at $49 to $80. That is NDSC's product, not an NDDOT category. NDDOT takes off 3 points either way.

NDSC's online page warns that most courts "mandate classroom attendance" for students a court has ordered to take a course. If a judge ordered yours, ask that court which formats it accepts before you pay.

## Is there an 8-hour course?

Not on NDDOT's list. North Dakota doesn't require 8 hours for point reduction, and no listed provider sells an 8-hour course as its NDDOT course. People search for one because other states require 8 hours for some courses. If a court or an employer told you 8 hours, that is their requirement, so ask them which course they accept.

## What is the insurance list?

A different list, kept by a different agency. [NDCC 26.1-25-04.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t26-1c25.pdf) requires insurers to reduce premiums for at least two years (three years for drivers 55 and older) after an accident prevention course "approved by the superintendent of the state highway patrol." The statute sets no percentage.

The Highway Patrol publishes [online](https://www.statepatrol.nd.gov/insurance-premium-reduction-online-courses) and [classroom](https://www.statepatrol.nd.gov/insurance-premium-reduction-classroom-courses) lists, approved through August 31, 2027 unless noted. Some providers are on both lists. Nine on NDDOT's list are not on the Highway Patrol's, and six on the Highway Patrol's are not on NDDOT's. Ours is not on the Highway Patrol's list today, so don't buy it for an insurance premium reduction. [More on insurance](/north-dakota/blog/does-defensive-driving-lower-insurance-north-dakota).

## How do I pick one?

Every course on NDDOT's list does the same thing for your points: 3 off, once every 12 months, or up to 5 kept off a new ticket if you elected the course at court. So the choice comes down to a few practical questions.

- Price. The numbers above are what each provider said on October 5. Check for add-ons before you pay.
- Points, insurance or both. For points, any NDDOT-approved course works. For an insurance premium reduction, pick one that is also on the Highway Patrol's list and ask your insurer first.
- Your deadline. If you elected the course when you posted bond, NDDOT must have your certificate within 30 days of telling the court ([NDCC 39-06.1-10.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)). A classroom date five weeks out won't fit. [The 30-day deadline](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-in-lieu-of-points-30-day-deadline).
- Classroom or online. Classroom options on the list are NDSC in Bismarck, Fargo and Minot, and TrainND in Williston. Everything else is online.

Whichever you pick, you send the certificate to NDDOT yourself, by email to drs@nd.gov. [How to send it](/north-dakota/blog/send-defensive-driving-certificate-to-nddot).

## Who shouldn't buy any course?

- A driver whose only ticket carries no points. Up to 10 mph over where the limit is 65 or less is 0 points, and so is up to 5 over where the limit is above 65 ([NDCC 39-06.1-10](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)).

## Is there traffic school in North Dakota?

Not by that name. The statute says "a driver training course approved by the director," meaning NDDOT's director ([NDCC 39-06.1-13](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)). NDDOT lists them under "Defensive Driving Courses" on its [points reduction page](https://www.dot.nd.gov/driver/driver-education/driver-license-points-reduction-and-points-schedule). A couple of providers on that list have "traffic school" in their names. The name doesn't matter. The NDDOT approval does.

## What does the course do?

Two things, and you use one or the other for a given ticket.

| Use | When | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 3-point reduction | After points are on your record | 3 points off |
| In lieu of points | When you post bond on a new ticket | Up to 5 points never entered |

The 3-point reduction works once in any 12 months and no more than 9 points in three years. It comes only from points you already had when you finished ([NDCC 39-06.1-13(2)](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)).

The in-lieu election is for a ticket worth 5 points or fewer. You tell the clerk in writing when you post bond, within 14 days of the citation, and NDDOT needs the certificate within 30 days after that ([NDCC 39-06.1-10.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)). It's limited to once in 12 months, and it "forfeits any point reduction option under section 39-06.1-13." [How to elect it](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## Will it get my ticket dismissed?

No. The bond "is forfeited even though an election is made," and the court's own guide says that by electing, "the person admits they committed the non-criminal traffic violation" ([ND Legal Self Help Center](https://www.ndcourts.gov/Media/Default/Legal%20Resources/Legal%20Self%20Help/Other%20Forms/Administrative-Traffic-Elect-Driving-Course.pdf)). The fee stays the same. You pay the ticket and the course.

## How does the online version work?

You sign up with your name, date of birth and North Dakota license number, then work through it in a browser. Ours is eight modules and a 25-question final quiz; 18 correct passes, and retakes are free and unlimited. It runs on a phone and saves your place. The certificate is a PDF you download the moment you pass.

Then you email it to drs@nd.gov. No provider reports completions to NDDOT for you. [Sending the certificate](/north-dakota/blog/send-defensive-driving-certificate-to-nddot).

## Is there a deadline?

Only if you elected the course at court. Then it's 30 days from the day you notified the clerk. For the 3-point reduction, the statute sets no deadline.

## Who shouldn't bother?

- Your ticket is 0 points, such as 10 over where the limit is 65 or less.
- You have 1 point. It comes off by itself after three months with no new points.
- You already used the reduction or the election in the last 12 months.
- You're at 12 points or more. The reduction is applied after the suspension, not instead of it.

## Does it lower my insurance?

That's a separate approval. North Dakota's insurance premium reduction law requires a course approved by the superintendent of the Highway Patrol ([NDCC 26.1-25-04.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t26-1c25.pdf)), not NDDOT. Ours isn't on the Highway Patrol's list. [Defensive driving and insurance](/north-dakota/blog/does-defensive-driving-lower-insurance-north-dakota).

## What is our course?

The North Dakota Defensive Driving Course: 4 hours, online, $24.99 with the certificate. NDDOT approved it on September 29, 2026; NDDOT's web list hadn't been updated to show it as of October 5. [Start the course](/north-dakota).

## What does a defensive driving course do in North Dakota?

It lowers your point total, or it keeps new points from being added. These are two separate options in state law, and you pick one for each course you take.

| | 3-point reduction | In lieu of points |
|---|---|---|
| What it does | Takes 3 points off your record | Keeps a new ticket's points off your record |
| When you choose | Any time you have points | At court, when you post bond |
| Which tickets | Points already on your record | A violation worth 5 points or fewer |
| Deadline | None | Certificate to NDDOT within 30 days of your election |
| How often | Once in any 12 months | Once in any 12 months |
| Law | NDCC 39-06.1-13 | NDCC 39-06.1-10.1 |

## How does the 3-point reduction work?

You finish an approved course and mail or deliver the certificate to NDDOT. The law says your point total "must, during any twelve-month period, be reduced by three points" when the director receives it.

Two limits apply. The reduction comes only from points you had before you finished the course. And it can't exceed 9 points in any three-year period.

## How does "in lieu of points" work?

You tell the court you elect a driver training course when you post bond for the ticket. If NDDOT gets proof that you finished within 30 days of that election, the points for the ticket are not assessed.

You still forfeit the bond, so the ticket costs the same. The violation has to be worth 5 points or fewer. [How to elect it at court](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election) has the steps.

## Which one should I use?

Use the in-lieu option if you just got a ticket and haven't posted bond yet. Use the reduction if the points are already on your record. [Reduction or in lieu of points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-point-reduction-vs-in-lieu-of-points) compares them with examples.

## Does the course have to be approved?

Yes. Both laws require a course "approved by the director" of NDDOT. NDDOT lists approved courses on its points reduction page.

## Who sends the certificate?

You do. North Dakota has no system for course providers to report completions. Email the certificate to drs@nd.gov or mail it to the Driver License Division, 608 East Boulevard Avenue, Bismarck, ND 58505-0700. See [how to send your certificate to NDDOT](/north-dakota/blog/send-defensive-driving-certificate-to-nddot).

## Will the course stop a suspension?

No. North Dakota suspends at 12 points. If your record has 12 or more when NDDOT receives the certificate, the reduction is applied after you serve the suspension. The course helps most when you take it at 8, 9 or 10 points.

## Do points go away without a course?

Yes. NDDOT takes 1 point off for every three months you go without new points. [How long points stay](/north-dakota/blog/how-long-points-stay-on-north-dakota-license) explains the timing.

## What does our course involve?

Four hours online, eight modules and a 25-question final with unlimited retakes. It's $24.99 with the certificate included. [What to expect](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-what-to-expect).

## What is the difference?

The reduction subtracts. The in-lieu election prevents. With the reduction, NDDOT takes 3 points off a total you already have. With the election, the points for one new ticket are never added.

## When is the in-lieu election better?

When the ticket is worth more than 3 points. A ticket for 21 to 25 mph over the limit is 5 points in a zone posted at 65 or less. Elect the course and none of the 5 are added. Let the points post and take the course later, and you get 3 back.

It's also better when you're close to 12. At 9 points, a 3-point ticket takes you to 12 and a suspension. The election keeps you at 9.

## When is the reduction better?

- The points are already on your record.
- The ticket is worth 6 points or more, which rules out the election.
- You used the election in the last 12 months.
- You missed the chance to elect at court.
- You don't want a 30-day deadline.

## Can I use both in the same year?

Not from the same course. NDCC 39-06.1-10.1 says a person making the election "forfeits any point reduction option under section 39-06.1-13." Each option is also limited to once in 12 months.

If you think you need both within a year, call NDDOT at 701-328-2604 before you decide and ask how they'll apply it to your record.

## What does each one cost?

The same. You pay the ticket either way, because the bond is forfeited even when you elect the course. You pay for the course either way. Ours is $24.99.

## What are the deadlines?

| | Deadline |
|---|---|
| In lieu of points | Certificate at NDDOT within 30 days of the day you notify the court |
| 3-point reduction | None |

## Three examples

**You have 2 points and get a ticket for 12 over in a 55 zone.** That's 1 point. Neither option matters much. Points drop by 1 every three months on their own.

**You have 6 points and get a ticket for 22 over in a 55 zone.** That's 5 points. Elect the course at court and you stay at 6.

**You have 10 points and no new ticket.** Take the course now and send in the certificate. You go to 7.

## What should I do next?

If you have a new ticket, read [how to elect the course at court](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election) before you post bond. If not, [check your points](/north-dakota/blog/check-points-north-dakota-driving-record) and [take the course](/north-dakota).

|---|---|

| 26 to 30 | 10 |

Yes. North Dakota suspends at 12 points. One ticket for 36 over in a 55 zone, or 31 over where the limit is above 65, is 12 points. The suspension is 7 days at 12 points and 7 more days for each point above that.

A defensive driving course takes 3 off, once every 12 months. Points also drop by 1 for every three months without new points.

Look at the posted limit where you were stopped. The higher table applies on a highway "on which the speed limit is posted in excess of sixty-five miles an hour."

posts.content:
## How is a North Dakota speeding fee calculated?

NDCC 39-06.1-06 sets it: "a fee of twenty dollars, or three dollars for each mile per hour over the limit, whichever is greater." An additional $20 is assessed at 16 mph or more over the limit.

On a highway posted above 65, the rate is $5 for each mile per hour, with the same $20 minimum and the same $20 added at 16 over.

## What does that come to?

| Miles per hour over | Limit 65 or less | Limit above 65 |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | $20 | $25 |
| 10 | $30 | $50 |
| 15 | $45 | $75 |
| 16 | $68 | $100 |
| 20 | $80 | $120 |
| 25 | $95 | $145 |
| 30 | $110 | $170 |

We worked these out from the statute. Your citation shows the amount you owe. A city ordinance can set a different amount.

## What about a school zone?

$40 for 1 to 10 mph over the posted speed. Above that, $40 plus $1 for each additional mile per hour, unless the regular fee would be higher.

## What about a work zone?

$150 for 1 to 10 mph over, then $150 plus $2 for each mile per hour over 10. This applies only when workers are present and the sign says "Minimum Fee $150."

## Is the fee the same as the bond?

Yes. The law says the bond "must be identical to the statutory fee." You can pay the fee, or post the bond and forfeit it. The amount is the same.

## What else does the ticket cost?

Points, if you were more than 10 over (or more than 5 over where the limit is above 65). Twelve points suspends your license, and reinstatement after a points suspension is $50. [Speeding ticket points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-points) has the schedule.

## Can a course lower the fee?

No. If you elect a driver training course in lieu of points, the bond "is forfeited even though an election is made." The course keeps the points off. You also pay for the course. Ours is $24.99.

## What if I don't pay?

If you do nothing, you're deemed to have admitted the violation. Failing to appear without paying the fee or posting bond is a class B misdemeanor, and NDDOT charges a $50 reinstatement fee for a suspension for failing to appear or post bond.

## How many points and how much is each violation?

Points come from [NDCC 39-06.1-10](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf). Fees come from [NDCC 39-06.1-06](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf), which sets the amount for a noncriminal ticket you pay without going to trial. The bond on your citation is the same amount. The last column shows whether you can elect a course in lieu of points, which is limited to noncriminal violations worth 5 points or fewer.

| Violation | Points | Fee | In lieu? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Failing to dim headlights | 1 | $20 | Yes |
| Child not in a restraint or seatbelt | 1 | $25 | Yes |
| Running a red light or other signal | 2 | $20 | Yes |
| Signal violation, not yielding to a pedestrian | 2 | $50 | Yes |
| Stop sign or yield sign | 2 | $40 | Yes |
| Not moving over for a stopped emergency vehicle | 2 | $50 | Yes |
| Other failure to yield right of way | 2 | $20 | Yes |
| Driving on the wrong side of the road | 2 | $20 | Yes |
| Overtaking where prohibited | 2 | $20 | Yes |
| Failing to use the care required | 2 | $30 | Yes |
| Disregarding a police officer's commands | 2 | $20 | Yes |
| Knowingly driving with defective brakes or equipment | 2 | $20 | Yes |
| Hazardous materials rules (39-21-44) | 2 | $250 | Yes |
| Exhibition driving | 3 | see citation | Yes |
| Failing to stop at a railroad crossing | 3 | $50 | Yes |
| Careless driving | 6 | $30 | No |
| Passing a stopped school bus | 6 | $250 | No |
| Driving without liability insurance | 6 | $150 ($300 if second in 3 years) | No |
| No insurance, second time in 18 months | 12 | $300 | No |
| No insurance, found after a crash | 14 | $150 or $300 | No |
| Racing | 10 | see citation | No |
| Reckless driving | 8 | criminal, set by the court | No |
| Aggravated reckless driving | 12 | criminal, set by the court | No |
| Leaving the scene, property damage | 14 | criminal, set by the court | No |
| Leaving the scene, injury or death | 18 | criminal, set by the court | No |
| Fleeing a peace officer | 24 | criminal, set by the court | No |

"See citation" means 39-06.1-06 doesn't name a fee for that violation; the amount on your ticket controls. Careless driving has a wrinkle: 39-06.1-06(2)(i) says $30, while the careless driving section itself names a different figure. [Careless driving tickets](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-careless-driving-ticket) covers the conflict. A city ordinance ticket can also carry a different amount than the state fee.

## How are speeding points and fees figured?

| Limit | Points | Fee |
|---|---|---|
| 65 or less | 0 up to 10 over, then 1 to 15 | $3 per mph over, $20 minimum |
| Above 65 | 0 up to 5 over, then 1 to 15 | $5 per mph over, $20 minimum |
| School zone | Same as above | $40 for 1 to 10 over, then $1 per mph |
| Work zone, workers present | Same as above | $150 for 1 to 10 over, then $2 per mph |

Add $20 at 16 mph or more over. On a 65-or-less road you can elect the course up to 25 over (5 points). Above 65, up to 20 over. [Speeding ticket points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-points) has the full band table, and [speeding ticket cost](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-cost) works out the dollars.

## Which violations carry no points?

- Driving without a license: 0 points, but a $150 fee under 39-06.1-06(9)
- Overtime and double parking under city ordinances
- Speeding up to 10 over where the limit is 65 or less, and up to 5 over where it's higher

NDDOT's [points page](https://www.dot.nd.gov/driver/driver-education/driver-license-points-reduction-and-points-schedule) says that for violations not on the schedule, "no points are assigned." [Tickets with no points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-tickets-with-no-points) lists more.

## Which points can a course keep off?

Those from a noncriminal violation worth 5 points or fewer, if you tell the court you're electing the course at the time you post bond, under [NDCC 39-06.1-10.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf). Offenses worth 6 or more are excluded. So are those listed in 39-06.1-05, including reckless driving, leaving the scene and driving under suspension. You still pay the fee in the table. Don't pay online if you want this; the election goes to the clerk in writing. [How the election works](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## Which points can a course take off afterward?

Any of them. The 3-point reduction under 39-06.1-13 comes off your total regardless of which violation put the points there. It's limited to once in 12 months and 9 points in three years, and it's lost if you made an in-lieu election. Our [4-hour course is $24.99](/north-dakota).

## What happens at 12 points?

NDDOT suspends your license for 7 days for each point over 11. Drivers under 18 lose their license at 6. [The points hub](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-suspension-three-point-reduction) has the suspension table and the removal rules.

Last reviewed October 5, 2026 against NDCC chapter 39-06.1 and NDDOT's points reduction page.

posts.content:
## How do points come off in North Dakota?

One at a time. NDCC 39-06.1-13 tells the director to reduce your total "by one point for each three-month period during which points are not recorded against the licensee's driving record."

Four points take a year to clear. Eight take two years.

## When does the three months start?

On the date your last points were entered. NDDOT bases the reduction date on the date the violation is entered, which can be later than the day you got the ticket.

## What stops the clock?

New points. A new moving violation restarts the three-month count from the date those points are entered.

A suspension also stops it. NDDOT says that if you're serving a suspension or cancellation for points, "points will not be reduced until the period of suspension is complete."

## How can I get them off faster?

Take an approved defensive driving course and send NDDOT the certificate. That's 3 points, once in any 12-month period, and up to 9 points in three years. It stacks with the automatic reduction.

Start at 9 points. With the course you're at 6 right away. Three months later you're at 5.

## Does the ticket stay on my record after the points are gone?

Yes, for a while. NDDOT's limited driving record leaves out violations and convictions more than three years old. The complete record includes them.

## What is my total after a suspension?

Eleven. After you complete a points suspension, the director reduces your total to 11. One more point and you're suspended again, so that's the time to take the course.

## How do I see where I stand?

Order a limited record online for $3. It shows your current point total. [How to check your points](/north-dakota/blog/check-points-north-dakota-driving-record).

posts.content:
## How do I see my points online?

Use NDDOT's Drivers License Record Request System. You enter your name, date of birth and driver ID, pay $3 by card, and the record appears on screen. Print it or send it to an email address before you close the window. NDDOT says that once you close the application you can't reprint or re-email it.

## What is on the limited record?

Your current point total and your recent history. NDDOT says a limited record leaves out:

- The date your license was first issued
- Violations and convictions more than three years old
- Suspensions, revocations and cancellations that were satisfied more than three years ago
- Crash information

For counting points, the limited record is enough.

## How do I get the complete record?

Fill out form SFN 51386, Request for Driver Abstract, and mail it with the $3 fee to:

Driver License Division
608 E. Boulevard Ave
Bismarck, ND 58505-0700

The complete record includes older violations and crash information.

## What should I look for?

- **Your point total.** Twelve suspends your license. For a driver under 18, six cancels it.
- **The date your last points were entered.** One point comes off for every three months after that date without new points.
- **Whether a recent ticket has posted yet.** Points are entered when NDDOT receives the report from the court.

## I sent in a course certificate. When should I check?

Give NDDOT a couple of weeks, then order a limited record. Your total should be 3 lower. If it isn't, call the Driver License Division at 701-328-2604. The office answers Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 9 to 3.

## When is the best time to take the course?

When the reduction will do the most. If you have 3 or more points, the course takes off 3. If you have 1 or 2, waiting three to six months clears them for free. If you're at 9 or more, take it now. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

posts.content:
## Where do I send my certificate?

NDDOT says approved courses are "submitted to DRS@ND.GOV." Email the PDF as an attachment. You can also mail a copy to:

NDDOT Driver License Division
608 East Boulevard Avenue
Bismarck, ND 58505-0700

## Why doesn't the course provider send it?

North Dakota has no reporting system for providers. The law puts it on the driver: the reduction happens "when the licensee mails or delivers a certificate to the director." We don't send yours, and no other provider sends theirs.

## What should the email say?

Keep it short, and put your identifying details in the message:

> Subject: Defensive driving certificate, [your full name]
>
> Attached is my certificate of completion for an approved defensive driving course. Please apply it to my record [as a 3-point reduction / for my in-lieu election made on (date) in (court)].
>
> Name as on license:
> Date of birth:
> Driver license number:
> Phone:

Say which of the two you want. If you elected the course at court, give the date and the court.

## Is there a deadline?

For the 3-point reduction, no.

For an in-lieu election, yes. The points are kept off only "if proof of completion of the course is presented to the department within thirty days after the individual notifies the court of the election." Send it the day you pass. [The 30-day deadline](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-in-lieu-of-points-30-day-deadline).

## How do I know NDDOT got it?

Keep the sent email. After a couple of weeks, order a $3 limited record online and look at your point total. If nothing changed, call 701-328-2604.

## Where do I get the certificate?

From your course. Ours is ready to download from your account as a PDF the moment you pass the final quiz, and we email you the link. One duplicate is free within 30 days if you lose it.

## What if I have 12 or more points?

Send it anyway. NDDOT applies the 3-point reduction after you serve the suspension.

posts.content:
## When does the 30 days start?

When you notify the court of your election, which you do when you post bond. The statute says the points may not be assessed "if proof of completion of the course is presented to the department within thirty days after the individual notifies the court of the election."

The clock doesn't start when you enroll, and it doesn't start when you finish.

## What has to happen inside the 30 days?

Two things: you finish the course, and NDDOT has your proof of completion. Finishing on day 29 and mailing the certificate on day 30 is too late if it arrives on day 33.

## What if I miss it?

The points are entered as if you hadn't elected the course. You've already forfeited the bond.

You can still use the course for a 3-point reduction later, but check with NDDOT first. The law says a person making the election forfeits the reduction option, so call 701-328-2604 and ask how they'll treat your certificate.

## How long does the course take?

Four hours. Ours is self-paced and saves your place. Most people finish in one or two evenings.

## What is a safe schedule?

| When | What to do |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Post bond, tell the court you elect the course, and enroll |
| Days 2 to 7 | Finish the four hours and pass the final |
| Same day you pass | Email the certificate to drs@nd.gov |
| Day 21 | Order a $3 limited record and confirm the points aren't there |

## Should I mail it or email it?

Email. It arrives the same day and you have a record of when you sent it. NDDOT's address for certificates is drs@nd.gov.

## I posted bond by mail. Did I make the election?

Only if you told the court. The law says you "must so notify the court at the time of posting the bond." If you posted bond without saying so, call the clerk of the court on your citation right away and ask whether the election can still be recorded.

## Is there a deadline for the 3-point reduction?

No. That one has no time limit. Only the in-lieu election does.

posts.content:
## What makes a ticket qualify?

NDCC 39-06.1-10.1 lets you elect a driver training course "in lieu of entry of points" and says the "point penalty of five points or fewer" is then not assessed. Three things rule it out:

1. You made the same election within the 12 months before this ticket was issued.
2. The offense is assigned 6 or more points.
3. The offense is one listed in section 39-06.1-05.

## Which speeding tickets qualify?

| Posted limit | Qualifies up to | Points at that speed |
|---|---|---|
| 65 or less | 25 mph over | 5 |
| Above 65 | 20 mph over | 5 |

Faster than that, the ticket is worth 7 or 9 points and doesn't qualify.

## Which other tickets qualify?

The ordinary 1-point, 2-point and 3-point violations:

- Failing to yield
- Disobeying a traffic signal or sign
- Driving on the wrong side of the road
- Overtaking where prohibited
- Failing to use the care required
- Failing to stop at a railroad crossing
- Exhibition driving

## Which tickets don't qualify?

| Violation | Points |
|---|---|
| Careless driving | 6 |
| Passing a school bus | 6 |
| Driving without liability insurance | 6, 12 or 14 |
| Racing | 10 |
| Reckless driving | 8 |
| Leaving the scene of an accident | 14 or 18 |
| Driving under the influence | Handled separately |
| Driving while suspended or revoked | Handled separately |

## My ticket has 0 points. Should I elect the course?

No. There's nothing to keep off, and you'd use up your one election for the year. Ten over in a 55 zone is 0 points.

## My ticket doesn't qualify. What can I do?

Let the points post, then use the 3-point reduction. It works on your total, whatever the points came from. Careless driving is 6 points, and a course brings that to 3.

## Does the court have to agree?

The statute says the individual "may appear before the court and elect" the course. You have to notify the court when you post bond. [How to elect it at court](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## How do I know how many points my ticket is worth?

Match the violation on your citation to the schedule. [Points by violation](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-by-violation) and [speeding ticket points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-points) have both tables.

posts.content:
## How often can I get the 3-point reduction?

Once in any 12-month period. NDCC 39-06.1-13 also says the reduction "may not exceed nine points during any three-year period commencing on the date of entry of the last points" against your record. That's three courses in three years at most.

## How often can I elect a course in lieu of points?

Once in 12 months. You can't elect if you made an election "within the twelve months preceding the date of issuance of the summons or notice to appear." The date that counts is the date on the new ticket.

## Can I use one of each in the same year?

The law says a person who makes the in-lieu election "forfeits any point reduction option under section 39-06.1-13." If you need both within a year, call NDDOT at 701-328-2604 and ask how they'll apply it before you pay for a second course.

## What is the most I can take off in a year?

| Source | Points off in 12 months |
|---|---|
| One course | 3 |
| Time, with no new points | 4 |
| Total | 7 |

The automatic reduction is 1 point for every three months without new points, and it has no yearly limit.

## When in the year should I take the course?

When you have at least 3 points to remove, and before you're at 12. The reduction comes only from points you had before you finished the course, so taking it at 1 point wastes most of it.

## Does the course expire?

The statute doesn't give a time limit for sending in a certificate for the 3-point reduction. Send it when you finish. A certificate in a drawer does nothing for your record.

## I took the course 11 months ago. Should I take it again now?

Wait until the 12 months have passed, then take it and send it in. If you're close to 12 points and can't wait, call NDDOT and ask for the exact date your last reduction was applied.

posts.content:
## How many points suspend a license in North Dakota?

Twelve. When your record reaches 12 or more, NDDOT notifies you that it intends to suspend your license, and you have the chance to ask for a hearing.

## How long is the suspension?

| Point total | Suspension |
|---|---|
| 12 | 7 days |
| 13 | 14 days |
| 14 | 21 days |
| 15 | 28 days |
| 18 | 49 days |

The rule in NDCC 39-06.1-10 is 7 days for each point over 11.

## How do I get my license back?

Serve the suspension and pay the reinstatement fee. NDDOT lists the fee for "Accumulation of 12 or More Points" at $50. You can pay online, by phone at 701-328-2604, or by mail to the Driver License Division, 608 E. Blvd Ave, Bismarck, ND 58505.

NDDOT's online system shows your outstanding requirements, so check it before you pay.

## What is my point total afterward?

Eleven. NDCC 39-06.1-12 has the director reduce your total to 11 when you complete the suspension. The law adds that a suspension "must be ordered if that licensee's point total again reaches twelve or more points."

One point, and you're suspended again.

## Will a defensive driving course stop the suspension?

No. If your record has 12 or more points when NDDOT receives your certificate, the 3-point reduction is applied after you serve the suspension.

Take the course anyway. After the suspension you're at 11, and the reduction puts you at 8.

## Can I drive to work while suspended?

Maybe. NDDOT can issue a temporary restricted license, which it also calls a work permit, to drivers 18 and older. It covers work, school and essential needs. You apply on form SFN 2254, and you have to serve part of the suspension with no driving first.

## What about drivers under 18?

The license is canceled at 6 points, and no work permit is available. See [under 18 and points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-under-18-points-license-cancellation).

## How do I stay out of this?

Take the course before you reach 12. At 9 or 10 points, a 3-point reduction is the margin that absorbs the next ticket. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

posts.description: A North Dakota driver under 18 loses the license at 6 points and starts over. What that means, and how a course helps before it happens.
posts.answer: If you're under 18 and reach 6 points, North Dakota cancels your permit or license. You start over as if you'd never had one: written test, permit, holding period, driver education and road test. No work permit is available. A defensive driving course takes 3 points off before you get there.

keyFacts.label: After cancellation
keyFacts.value: Start over with a new permit

faq.q: How many points can a driver under 18 have in North Dakota?
faq.a: Fewer than 6. At 6 or more points, a driver under 18 has the permit or license canceled.

faq.q: What happens when a teen license is canceled in North Dakota?
faq.a: The driver starts over as if never licensed: written and vision tests, parental permission, a new permit and holding period, and driver education before the road test.

faq.q: Can a driver under 18 get a work permit in North Dakota?
faq.a: No. NDDOT says drivers under 18 are not eligible for a temporary restricted license.

posts.content:
## What happens to a driver under 18 at 6 points?

The license is canceled. NDDOT says: "If you are under the age of 18 and accumulate six or more points on your driving record your permit or license will be cancelled."

## What does "canceled" mean?

You start again. NDDOT says you're "required to start all over again as if you have never had a permit or license before." That includes:

- The written test and vision test
- A parent's permission
- A new instruction permit
- Holding the permit at least 12 months if you're under 16, or at least 6 months if you're under 18
- Driver education before the road test

## How easy is it to reach 6 points?

One ticket can do it. Careless driving is 6 points. So is passing a stopped school bus. A speeding ticket for 21 to 25 over is 5 where the limit is 65 or less, and any 1-point ticket after that makes 6.

## Can a teen get a work permit?

No. NDDOT says youths under 18 are not eligible for a temporary restricted license.

## How does a defensive driving course help?

Two ways, the same as for adults.

**Before the points post.** For a ticket worth 5 points or fewer, the driver can elect a course at court when posting bond. If NDDOT has the certificate within 30 days, those points are never added.

**After the points post.** A course takes 3 points off, once in any 12 months.

## Does the course help after 6 points?

Not with the cancellation. The law says that if a minor's record has 6 points or more when NDDOT receives the certificate, the reduction is applied after the cancellation period.

## What should a parent do after a first ticket?

1. Find out how many points the ticket is worth. [Points by violation](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-by-violation).
2. If it's 5 or fewer and bond hasn't been posted, [elect the course at court](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).
3. If the points have already posted, have your teen take the course and email the certificate to drs@nd.gov.
4. Order a $3 record a few weeks later to confirm the total.

## What does our course involve?

Four hours online, on a phone or a computer. It's $24.99 with the certificate included. [What to expect](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-what-to-expect).

posts.title: Should you just pay your North Dakota traffic ticket?
posts.seoTitle: Should You Just Pay a North Dakota Ticket?
posts.description: Paying a North Dakota ticket admits the violation, and the points follow. What to tell the court when you post bond if you want them kept off.
posts.answer: Paying the fee or forfeiting your bond admits the violation, and the court reports it to NDDOT within 10 days. If the ticket is worth 5 points or fewer and you want the points kept off, tell the court you elect a driver training course at the time you post bond. After that, it's too late.

keyFacts.value: Elect the course when you post bond

faq.q: Is paying a ticket an admission of guilt in North Dakota?
faq.a: Paying the statutory fee or forfeiting bond is an admission of the violation under NDCC 39-06.1-02. The court certifies it to NDDOT within 10 days.

faq.q: How long do I have to pay a ticket in North Dakota?
faq.a: If you post bond by mail for a state-law citation, it must be submitted within 14 days of the date of the citation. Otherwise pay at or before the hearing time on the citation.

faq.q: What happens if I do not pay a North Dakota traffic ticket?
faq.a: You are deemed to have admitted the violation. Failing to appear without paying the fee or posting bond is a class B misdemeanor.

faq.q: Can I keep the points off after I have already paid?
faq.a: No. The election has to be made when you post bond. After the points post, a defensive driving course can take 3 of them off.

posts.content:
## What happens when I pay a North Dakota ticket?

You admit the violation. Most traffic tickets in North Dakota are noncriminal, and NDCC 39-06.1-02 gives you three ways to handle one:

1. Pay the statutory fee at or before the time set for your hearing.
2. Post bond and forfeit it by not appearing.
3. Ask for a hearing.

With the first two, the violation is admitted. The court certifies the admission to NDDOT within 10 days, and NDDOT enters the points.

## How long do I have?

If you post bond by mail for a state-law ticket, it has to be submitted within 14 days of the date of the citation. You mark on the citation whether you want a hearing. If you don't ask for one within the 14 days, the bond is forfeited and the violation admitted.

## How do I keep the points off?

Tell the court you elect a driver training course in lieu of points, and do it when you post bond. The law says the person "must so notify the court at the time of posting the bond." The violation has to be worth 5 points or fewer.

Don't pay online first. The state courts' payment site says "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT" if you want to take a defensive driving course instead of points. The election is made in writing to the clerk of court when you post bond, in person or by mail in the same envelope as the citation, within 14 days of the citation (ND Legal Self Help Center guide, rev. July 2024). There is no online way to elect it.

Then finish an approved course and get the certificate to NDDOT within 30 days. [How to elect it at court](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## Does electing the course lower what I pay?

No. The bond "is forfeited even though an election is made." You pay the ticket and the course.

## What happens at a hearing?

You can make a statement explaining what happened. The official can waive, reduce or suspend the fee or bond. If you follow that procedure, the law still treats you as having admitted the violation.

## When is it fine to just pay?

- The ticket has no points. Ten over in a 55 zone is 0 points and $30.
- The ticket is worth 1 point and your record is clean. It clears in three months.
- You've already used your election in the last 12 months.
- The ticket is worth 6 points or more, so the election isn't available. Pay it, then use the 3-point reduction.

## What if I ignore the ticket?

You're deemed to have admitted the violation, and the court reports it. Failing to appear without paying the fee or posting bond is a class B misdemeanor. NDDOT lists a $50 reinstatement fee for a suspension for failing to appear or post bond.

## I already paid. Now what?

The points will post. Take a defensive driving course and send NDDOT the certificate for a 3-point reduction. There's no deadline on that one. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

posts.title: Does a defensive driving course lower your insurance in North Dakota?
posts.seoTitle: Does Defensive Driving Lower Insurance in ND?
posts.description: North Dakota has two lists of approved courses: NDDOT's for points and the Highway Patrol's for insurance. Which one our course is on.
posts.answer: It depends on which course you take. North Dakota approves courses for two separate purposes. NDDOT approves courses for point reduction. The Highway Patrol approves courses for insurance premium reduction. Our course is approved for points and is not on the Highway Patrol's insurance list, so take it for your record, not your premium.

faq.q: Does a defensive driving course lower insurance in North Dakota?
faq.a: It can, if the course is on the North Dakota Highway Patrol list of courses approved for insurance premium reduction and your insurer offers the reduction. That list is separate from the NDDOT list for points.

faq.q: Who approves defensive driving courses in North Dakota?
faq.a: NDDOT approves courses for point reduction. The North Dakota Highway Patrol approves courses for insurance premium reduction.

faq.q: Does in lieu of points remove the ticket from my record?
faq.a: No. It keeps the points from being assessed. The law does not say the violation is removed from the record.

posts.content:
## Are there two kinds of approved course?

Yes. NDDOT lists the courses approved for a 3-point reduction on its points page. The North Dakota Highway Patrol keeps a separate list of courses approved for insurance premium reduction, and says its online courses are approved through August 31, 2027.

Some providers are on both lists. Being on one doesn't put a course on the other.

## Which approval does our course have?

NDDOT's, for points. We checked the Highway Patrol's list of online insurance courses on September 29, 2026, and we're not on it.

If a lower premium is your only reason for taking a course, choose one from the Highway Patrol's list, and confirm with your insurer first.

## What should I ask my insurer?

- Do you lower my premium for a defensive driving course?
- Does the course have to be on the Highway Patrol's list?
- How long does the reduction last?
- Do you look at my points, my violations, or both?

## Can fewer points help my insurance?

We can't promise it. Insurers set their own rules, and the violation stays on your driving record even when points are reduced or kept off.

Fewer points do keep you away from a suspension. Twelve points suspends your license, and a suspension on your record is something most drivers want to avoid for reasons beyond the premium.

## Will keeping a ticket's points off hide the ticket?

No. Electing a course in lieu of points keeps the points from being assessed. The law doesn't say the violation is removed.

## So who should take our course?

A driver who has points and wants 3 of them gone, or a driver with a new ticket worth 5 points or fewer who elected the course at court. For those two jobs it's four hours and $24.99. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

## How long is the course?

Four hours. You can do it in one sitting or spread it out. Most people finish in one or two evenings.

## What does it cover?

Eight modules:

1. Introduction and orientation
2. Traffic laws and why they matter
3. Defensive driving techniques
4. The psychology of driving
5. Impaired driving
6. Sharing the road, including farm equipment and winter traffic
7. Crash dynamics and avoidance
8. The vehicle and driving environment, including North Dakota's rules and point system

Then the final quiz.

## Are there quizzes?

A short one after each of the first seven modules. It's three questions, and you need all three right to move on. You can try as many times as you need, and the correct answers are shown.

## What is the final quiz like?

Twenty-five questions. Eighteen correct passes. If you miss it, you can retake it right away with different questions. There's no limit and no charge.

## Will I be asked to prove who I am?

Yes, briefly. You answer a few personal-history questions when you start and again before the final quiz. That confirms the person finishing the course is the person who enrolled.

## Can I do it on my phone?

Yes. The course and exam work in a phone's browser, and your progress saves when you leave. You can switch between a phone and a computer.

## What do I need to enroll?

- Your name, date of birth and North Dakota driver license number, as they appear on your license
- A card for the $24.99

## What do I get when I pass?

A certificate of completion, ready to download from your account as a PDF the moment you pass. We also email you the link.

Then you send it to NDDOT. We don't report completions, and no provider does in North Dakota. [How to send your certificate](/north-dakota/blog/send-defensive-driving-certificate-to-nddot).

## Is there a deadline to finish?

Not from us, and not for the 3-point reduction. If you elected the course at court in lieu of points, NDDOT needs your certificate [within 30 days of the election](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-in-lieu-of-points-30-day-deadline).

## What if I change my mind?

You get a full refund any time before you complete the course. After you pass and the certificate is issued, there's no refund.

## Who do I call with a problem?

Support is by phone at (888) 885-5707 and by email at info@roadreadysafety.com.

posts.title: Driving without insurance in North Dakota: points and fees
posts.seoTitle: ND No Insurance Ticket: Points and Fees
posts.description: A North Dakota no-insurance ticket is 6 points and $150. A second one within 18 months is 12 points, which suspends your license on its own.
posts.answer: Driving without liability insurance is 6 points and a $150 fee in North Dakota. A second violation within 18 months is 12 points, and the fee for a second violation within three years is $300. If the violation is found after a crash in which the driver owns the vehicle, it's 14 points.

keyFacts.label: Found after a crash, driver is owner

faq.q: How many points is driving without insurance in North Dakota?
faq.a: Six points. It is 12 points with a prior violation in the last 18 months, and 14 points if found in the investigation of a crash in which the driver is the owner.

faq.q: How much is a no insurance ticket in North Dakota?
faq.a: $150 for a first violation and $300 for a second or later violation within three years, under NDCC 39-06.1-06.

faq.q: Can defensive driving remove no insurance points in North Dakota?
faq.a: A course can take 3 points off your total afterward. The in-lieu election at court is not available, because the violation is worth 6 points or more.

posts.content:
## How many points is a no-insurance ticket?

| Situation | Points |
|---|---|
| Driving without liability insurance | 6 |
| Same, with a prior violation in the last 18 months | 12 |
| Found in the investigation of a crash, and the driver is the owner | 14 |

These are in NDCC 39-06.1-10.

## What is the fee?

$150 for a first violation. $300 for a second or later violation within three years. Both are set in NDCC 39-06.1-06.

## Can a no-insurance ticket suspend my license by itself?

Yes. Twelve points is a 7-day suspension. Fourteen points is 21 days. NDDOT also lists a $50 reinstatement fee for failing to maintain liability insurance.

## Can I take a course to keep these points off?

Not at court. The in-lieu election is for violations worth 5 points or fewer, and this one starts at 6.

## Can I take a course to reduce them afterward?

Yes. The 3-point reduction works on your total. After a first violation you'd go from 6 to 3.

If you're at 12 or more when NDDOT receives your certificate, the reduction is applied after you serve the suspension.

## How long until the points are gone?

One point comes off for every three months without new points. Six points take 18 months to clear that way. With a course, 3 are gone as soon as NDDOT applies the certificate, and the other 3 clear in nine months.

## What should I do now?

1. Get insured and keep proof in the vehicle.
2. Respond to the citation by the date on it.
3. After the points post, take the course and email the certificate to drs@nd.gov.
4. Order a $3 record to confirm your total.

[How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

posts.content:
## What is the in-lieu election?

It's a choice the law gives you at court. NDCC 39-06.1-10.1 says a person cited for a traffic violation "may appear before the court and elect to attend a driver training course approved by the director in lieu of entry of points."

## How do I make the election?

1. **Check the points.** The violation has to be worth 5 or fewer. [Which tickets qualify](/north-dakota/blog/which-tickets-qualify-in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota).
2. **Contact the court on your citation** before you post bond. Ask the clerk how the court records an election.
3. **Post bond and say you elect the course.** The law says you "must so notify the court at the time of posting the bond."
4. **Write down the date.** Your 30 days run from it.
5. **Enroll in an approved course the same day.**

## What should I say to the clerk?

> I'm posting bond on citation [number]. I elect to attend a driver training course in lieu of points under section 39-06.1-10.1. How do you want me to note that?

Ask for something in writing that shows the election and the date.

## What do I do after I elect?

Finish the course and get the certificate to NDDOT. Email it to drs@nd.gov with your name, date of birth, license number, the court and the date of your election. NDDOT has to have it within 30 days of the election. [The 30-day deadline](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-in-lieu-of-points-30-day-deadline).

## What does it cost?

The bond, which equals the fee for the violation, and the course. The statute says you pay the course fee to the course sponsor. Ours is $24.99.

## When can't I elect?

- You made an election in the 12 months before this ticket was issued.
- The offense is assigned 6 or more points.
- The offense is one of those listed in NDCC 39-06.1-05, such as reckless driving, leaving the scene, or driving while suspended.

## Does the election use up my 3-point reduction?

The law says a person making the election "forfeits any point reduction option under section 39-06.1-13." See [reduction or in lieu of points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-point-reduction-vs-in-lieu-of-points).

## Want the course instead of points? Don't pay online

Don't pay online first. The state courts' payment site says "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT" if you want to take a defensive driving course instead of points. The election is made in writing to the clerk of court when you post bond, in person or by mail in the same envelope as the citation, within 14 days of the citation (ND Legal Self Help Center guide, rev. July 2024). There is no online way to elect it.

## Is this a dismissal?

No. The points aren't assessed. The bond is forfeited, and the law doesn't say the violation is removed from your record.

Points come off two ways: 1 for every three months with no new points, and 3 when you send NDDOT a certificate from an approved course, once every 12 months. faq.q: How many points suspends a license in North Dakota?
faq.a: Twelve. The suspension is 7 days for each point over 11, so 7 days at 12 points and 14 days at 13, under NDCC 39-06.1-10.

faq.q: How many points does a defensive driving course remove in North Dakota?
faq.a: Three, once in any 12-month period, up to 9 points in any three-year period. The reduction only comes off points that were on your record before you finished the course.

faq.q: Can I take the course now to cover a ticket I get later?
faq.a: No. NDCC 39-06.1-13 limits the reduction to points accumulated before completion. Points can't be banked, so take the course after the points are on your record.

faq.q: Can I use the in-lieu election and the 3-point reduction in the same year?
faq.a: The law says a driver who elects a course in lieu of points forfeits any point reduction option under 39-06.1-13. If you think you need both, call NDDOT at 701-328-2604 before you pay for a second course.

faq.q: Do my points go to zero after a suspension?
faq.a: No. NDCC 39-06.1-12 sets your total to 11 once you complete the suspension. Reaching 12 again means another suspension, so a single 1-point ticket would do it.
