posts.content:
## How does the North Dakota point system work?

Every violation has a point value fixed by [NDCC 39-06.1-10](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf). When a court reports a conviction, an admission or an adjudication, NDDOT enters "the proper points" on your driving record. The court doesn't choose the number and can't waive it. Bismarck's municipal court says so on its own FAQ: points are handled by the Drivers License Division.

At 12 points, NDDOT notifies you that it intends to suspend your license, and you get a chance at a hearing before the suspension is ordered.

## How many points is each violation?

This is the whole schedule in 39-06.1-10(3), in plain words. NDDOT's points page says that "for violations not listed, no points are assigned."

| Noncriminal violation | Points |
|---|---|
| Overtime or double parking (city ordinance) | 0 |
| Driving without a license | 0 |
| Not following highway patrol rules under 39-21-46(3) | 0 |
| Failing to display license plates | 1 |
| Parking in a prohibited place | 1 |
| Leaving a vehicle improperly unattended on an open highway | 1 |
| Opening doors when unsafe | 1 |
| Failing to dim headlights | 1 |
| Child not in a restraint system or seatbelt | 1 |
| Driving a modified vehicle (39-21-45.1) | 1 |
| Letting an unauthorized minor or person drive | 2 |
| Stopping or parking on an open highway | 2 |
| Knowingly driving with defective or unlawful equipment | 2 |
| Knowingly driving with defective brakes | 2 |
| Failing to yield right of way | 2 |
| Disobeying a traffic-control device | 2 |
| Driving on the wrong side of the road | 2 |
| Disregarding a police officer's lawful command | 2 |
| Overtaking where prohibited or unsafely | 2 |
| Failing to use the care required (39-09-01.1) | 2 |
| Motorcycle: passengers or packages, laned traffic, no passenger footrests, no helmet | 2 each |
| Driving in violation of 39-08-18 | 2 |
| Violating 39-21-44 (hazardous materials) | 2 |
| Violating an instruction permit's conditions | 2 |
| Exhibition driving | 3 |
| Failing to stop at a railroad crossing | 3 |
| Violating a restricted certificate (39-06.1-03) | 4 |
| Clinging to another vehicle on a motorcycle | 4 |
| Careless driving (39-09-01) | 6 |
| Passing a stopped school bus | 6 |
| Driving in violation of 39-08-09 | 6 |
| No liability insurance | 6 |
| Racing or drag racing | 10 |
| No insurance, second within 18 months | 12 |
| No insurance, found in a crash investigation, driver is the owner | 14 |

| Criminal violation | Points |
|---|---|
| Knowingly operating an unsafe vehicle | 2 |
| Causing a crash with an emergency or highway maintenance vehicle | 2 |
| Violating a corrective lens restriction | 3 |
| Violating any other license restriction | 4 |
| Reckless driving | 8 |
| Aggravated reckless driving | 12 |
| Leaving the scene, property damage | 14 |
| Leaving the scene, injury or death | 18 |
| Fleeing a peace officer | 24 |

Speeding has two schedules. Paragraph 30 covers roads posted 65 or less. Paragraph 33 covers roads posted above 65.

| Mph over | Limit 65 or less | Limit above 65 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 to 5 | 0 | 0 |
| 6 to 10 | 0 | 1 |
| 11 to 15 | 1 | 3 |
| 16 to 20 | 3 | 5 |
| 21 to 25 | 5 | 7 |
| 26 to 30 | 9 | 10 |
| 31 to 35 | 9 | 12 |
| 36 to 45 | 12 | 15 |
| 46 or more | 15 | 15 |

The fee for each of these is on [traffic violations: points and fees](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-by-violation).

## How do points come off?

Two ways, both in [NDCC 39-06.1-13](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf).

Time. NDDOT takes off 1 point "for each three-month period during which points are not recorded against the licensee's driving record." The clock runs from the date your last points were entered, so a new ticket restarts it.

A course. Your total "must, during any twelve-month period, be reduced by three points" when you mail or deliver a certificate from an approved driver training course. The same subsection sets the limits:

- The reduction comes "solely from a point total accumulated before completion." Points from a ticket you get next month aren't covered.
- It "may not exceed nine points during any three-year period."
- If you're at 12 or more (6 or more as a minor) when NDDOT receives the certificate, the reduction is applied after you serve the suspension or cancellation.

NDDOT's [points page](https://www.dot.nd.gov/driver/driver-education/driver-license-points-reduction-and-points-schedule) says the same in shorter form: a course reduces "total points by 3, once every 12 months." You send the certificate yourself to drs@nd.gov. [How to send it](/north-dakota/blog/send-defensive-driving-certificate-to-nddot).

| You have | After the course | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 2 | Room for two more 2-point tickets |
| 9 | 6 | A 5-point ticket no longer suspends you |
| 11 | 8 | You're no longer one point from a suspension |

## Can a course keep a new ticket's points off?

Yes, if the ticket is worth 5 points or fewer. [NDCC 39-06.1-10.1](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf) lets you elect an approved course "in lieu of entry of points." The conditions:

- You tell the court at the time you post bond. The court self-help guide gives you 14 days from the citation date to post it.
- The notice is written. Mail it in the same envelope as the citation, or hand it to the clerk when you pay in person.
- The bond is forfeited anyway. You pay the fee and the course.
- NDDOT must have your certificate within 30 days of the day you notified the court.
- Not available if you elected within the previous 12 months, if the offense is 6 points or more, or if it's an offense listed in 39-06.1-05 (reckless driving, leaving the scene, driving under suspension and others).
- Electing "forfeits any point reduction option under section 39-06.1-13."

There's no online path for the election. The North Dakota courts payment page opens with: "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT" if you have questions about taking a defensive driving course. Pay online first and the points post. [How the election works](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## What happens at 12 points?

A suspension of 7 days for each point over 11, under 39-06.1-10(2).

| Point total | Suspension |
|---|---|
| 12 | 7 days |
| 13 | 14 days |
| 14 | 21 days |
| 15 | 28 days |

The suspension starts 20 days after the order is delivered to your address on file. Reinstatement is $50. When you finish it, [39-06.1-12](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf) sets your total to 11, not zero, and a suspension "must be ordered" if you reach 12 again. One more 1-point ticket does it. [Suspended for points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-license-suspended-for-points).

## What about drivers under 18?

NDCC 39-06-01.1 cancels the license of a driver whose points from violations committed as a minor total "in excess of five points." Six points is enough. After cancellation the driver is treated as never having held a license and starts again with an instruction permit. [Under 18 and points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-under-18-points-license-cancellation).

## How do I check my points?

Order your record from NDDOT. It costs $3. [How to check your points](/north-dakota/blog/check-points-north-dakota-driving-record) covers the form and the difference between a limited and a complete record.

## Who shouldn't take the course?

- A driver with a 0-point ticket. Up to 10 over where the limit is 65 or less carries no points.
- A driver with 1 or 2 points and nothing else coming. Time removes a point every three months.
- A driver already at 12 or more. The reduction waits until the suspension is served.
- A driver who just elected a course in lieu of points. The statute says that election forfeits the 3-point option.

Everyone else between 3 and 11 points gets the full benefit. Ours is [4 hours online for $24.99](/north-dakota), certificate included, and you email it to drs@nd.gov when you pass the quiz.

Last reviewed October 5, 2026 against NDCC chapter 39-06.1 and NDDOT's points reduction page.

posts.content:
## What counts as careless driving?

Driving faster than is "reasonable and prudent under the conditions." NDCC 39-09-01 calls this the basic rule. It requires a safe speed at intersections, railroad crossings, curves and hill crests, on narrow or winding roads, and when weather, traffic or pedestrians create a hazard.

You can be cited for it while driving under the posted limit. Ice, fog and blowing snow are the usual reasons.

## How many points is it?

Six. That's in the point schedule at NDCC 39-06.1-10.

## What is the fee?

The two parts of the code don't match. NDCC 39-09-01 says a person guilty of careless driving "must be assessed a fee of one hundred dollars." The fee schedule in NDCC 39-06.1-06 lists a violation of section 39-09-01 at thirty dollars. We read both on September 29, 2026.

Pay the amount printed on your citation. If it looks wrong, ask the clerk of the court named on it.

## Can I elect a course to keep the points off?

No. The in-lieu election is for violations worth 5 points or fewer.

## What can a course do?

Take 3 points off afterward. Let the points post, finish an approved defensive driving course, and email the certificate to drs@nd.gov. You go from 6 to 3. The other 3 clear in nine months if you get no new points.

## When does careless driving become more serious?

When it injures certain people or damages certain equipment. It's an infraction, not a fee-only violation, if the careless driving:

- Injures the operator of snow removal equipment at work
- Injures a first responder, or someone in a stopped emergency vehicle with lights on, at the side of the road
- Injures a person helping someone stopped at the roadside with hazard lights on
- Causes more than $4,000 in damage to snow removal equipment or an emergency vehicle

## What about a driver under 18?

Six points cancels a license for a driver under 18. One careless driving ticket does it. See [under 18 and points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-under-18-points-license-cancellation).

## How is this different from reckless driving?

Reckless driving is a crime. Careless driving is a noncriminal violation you can resolve by paying the fee. See [reckless driving](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-reckless-driving-points).

posts.content:
## What is reckless driving in North Dakota?

NDCC 39-08-03 defines it as driving a vehicle:

1. "Recklessly in disregard of the rights or safety of others," or
2. "Without due caution and circumspection and at a speed or in a manner so as to endanger or be likely to endanger any person or the property of another."

## What is the penalty?

It's a class B misdemeanor. If the reckless driving "causes and inflicts injury upon the person of another," it's aggravated reckless driving, a class A misdemeanor. The court sets the sentence.

## How many points is it?

Eight for reckless driving and 12 for aggravated reckless driving. Twelve points is a 7-day suspension.

## Can I just pay the citation?

No. Reckless driving is one of the offenses listed in NDCC 39-06.1-05, which can't be handled by paying a fee or forfeiting bond. The Fargo Municipal Court tells drivers charged with a criminal traffic violation that they "must appear in court on the date and at the time noted."

Talk to an attorney before that date. We don't give legal advice.

## Can a course keep the points off?

No. The in-lieu election isn't available for an offense listed in section 39-06.1-05, or for one worth 6 points or more. Reckless driving is both.

## Can a course help afterward?

Yes. The 3-point reduction works on your total. After a reckless driving conviction on a clean record, you'd go from 8 to 5.

If your record has 12 or more points when NDDOT receives the certificate, the reduction is applied after the suspension.

## How long do the points last?

One point comes off for every three months without new points. Eight points take two years to clear that way. With a course, it's 15 months.

## How is careless driving different?

Careless driving is noncriminal and 6 points. See [careless driving](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-careless-driving-ticket).

posts.content:
## How many points is a stop sign ticket?

Two. Stop sign and yield sign violations fall under failing to yield the right of way in the point schedule.

## How many points is a red light ticket?

Two. It's scored as disobeying an official traffic-control device.

## What are the fees?

| Violation | State fee |
|---|---|
| Stop sign or yield sign (NDCC 39-10-24, 39-10-44) | $40 |
| Traffic signal (NDCC 39-10-05) | $20 |
| Traffic signal, failing to yield to a pedestrian | $50 |

These are the state fees in NDCC 39-06.1-06. A city ordinance can set a different amount, so check your citation.

## Where do I have to stop at a stop sign?

At the marked stop line. If there isn't one, before the crosswalk. If there's no crosswalk either, at "the point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic."

After stopping, you yield to any vehicle in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

## What does a yield sign require?

Slowing to a reasonable speed, and stopping if safety requires it. The law adds that if you pass a yield sign without stopping and collide with a vehicle in the intersection, the collision is "prima facie evidence" that you failed to yield.

## Can I keep the 2 points off?

Yes. Tell the court you elect a driver training course when you post bond, then get the certificate to NDDOT within 30 days. [How to elect it](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## Should I?

It depends on your record. Two points clear in six months without a course. You get one election every 12 months, and you may want it for a bigger ticket.

If you're at 10 points, use it. Two more is a suspension.

posts.content:
## When do I have to stop for a school bus?

When the bus is stopped on the highway with its flashing red lights on or the stop sign on its control arm out. NDCC 39-10-46 applies to a driver "meeting or overtaking from either direction."

## When can I go again?

When one of three things happens:

- The bus starts moving.
- The bus driver signals you to proceed.
- The red lights and stop arm are no longer in use.

## What do the amber lights mean?

The bus is about to stop. The driver can turn them on 300 to 500 feet before the stop. Slow down and be ready.

## Is there any time I don't have to stop?

Yes. On a highway with separate roadways, you don't have to stop for a bus on the other roadway. The same goes on a controlled-access highway when the bus is in a loading zone where pedestrians can't cross.

A painted center line or a turn lane is not a separate roadway.

## What is the penalty?

Six points and a $250 fee under state law. For a driver under 18, six points cancels the license.

## Can the vehicle's owner be cited?

Yes. NDCC 39-10-46.1 says a registered owner may not permit the vehicle to be used to pass a stopped school bus. If the vehicle is seen doing it, the law presumes the owner permitted it. The fee is also $250.

## Can a course keep the points off?

No. The violation is worth 6 points, and the in-lieu election stops at 5.

## What can I do afterward?

Take a defensive driving course and email the certificate to drs@nd.gov. That takes 3 points off, leaving 3, which clear in nine months without new points. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

posts.answer: Texting while driving is a $100 fee in North Dakota. It isn't on the state's point schedule, so no points are added. The ban covers composing, reading or sending electronic messages, including at a red light. Phone calls, GPS and hands-free use are allowed for adult drivers.

faq.q: How much is a texting while driving ticket in North Dakota?
Does a texting ticket put points on your license in North Dakota?
faq.a: No. Texting while driving is not on the point schedule, and NDDOT assigns no points for violations that are not listed.

faq.q: Can you text at a red light in North Dakota?
faq.a: No. The law treats a temporary stop at a traffic signal or sign as being in traffic.

faq.q: Can teens use a phone while driving in North Dakota?
faq.a: Drivers who are 16 or 17 with a class D license may not talk, text or read messages on a device while the vehicle is in motion, except in an emergency.

posts.content:
## What does the law ban?

Using a wireless communications device "to compose, read, or send an electronic message" while operating a vehicle that is part of traffic (NDCC 39-08-23). Electronic messages include texts, email, instant messages and requests to load a web page.

## Does it apply at a red light?

Yes. The law defines traffic to include "a temporary stop or halt of motion, such as at an official traffic-control signal or sign." A vehicle that is lawfully parked is not in traffic.

## What is still allowed?

- Entering or selecting a phone number to make or take a call
- Using GPS or a navigation system
- Talking on the phone
- Using a device in a voice-activated or hands-free way
- Using a device to get emergency help or report a crash, a medical emergency or a serious hazard

## What is the penalty?

A $100 fee. The violation isn't listed in the point schedule, and NDDOT says that for violations not listed, no points are assigned.

## What is the rule for teen drivers?

Stricter. A driver who is 16 or 17 with a class D license may not use an electronic communication device "to talk, compose, read, or send an electronic message" while the vehicle is in motion. The only exception is an emergency.

## What is "failure to maintain control"?

A separate $100 violation for distracted driving. NDCC 39-08-25 applies when a driver commits another traffic offense, or is in a reportable crash with property damage, while engaged in an activity that isn't needed to drive and that impairs safe driving. It can be cited along with the other offense.

## Do I need a course for a texting ticket?

No. There are no points to remove or keep off. Pay the fee by the date on the citation.

If the stop also produced a ticket that has points, such as speeding, that one is where a course matters. [Points by violation](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-by-violation).

posts.content:
## What does the seat belt law require?

Every occupant buckled. NDCC 39-21-41.4 says a driver may not operate a vehicle designed for fewer than eleven passengers "unless each occupant is wearing a properly adjusted and fastened safety belt."

## Can an officer stop me only for a seat belt?

The section of the code that limited seat belt enforcement, 39-21-41.5, was repealed in 2023.

## Who is exempt?

- Drivers of farm implements and operators of farm vehicles
- Rural mail carriers on duty
- An occupant with a medical or disabling condition, with a signed statement from a physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse
- Emergency medical personnel giving direct patient care
- Occupants when all the belts are already in use

## What is the penalty?

A $20 fee. The violation isn't on the point schedule, so no points are added.

## What are the rules for children?

| Child | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Under 8 | In a child restraint system, used as the manufacturer directs |
| Under 8, at least 57 inches tall | Correctly buckled in a safety belt |
| 8 through 17 | In a child restraint or correctly buckled in a safety belt |

A child restraint violation is a $25 fee and 1 point.

## Does a seat belt ticket count against me in a lawsuit?

The law says a violation "is not, in itself, evidence of negligence" and can't be used in any proceeding other than the one charging the violation.

## Do I need a course?

Not for a seat belt ticket. For the 1 point from a child restraint ticket, waiting three months clears it. A course makes sense when you have 3 or more points. [How long points stay](/north-dakota/blog/how-long-points-stay-on-north-dakota-license).

## Which tickets have no points?

| Violation | Points | State fee |
|---|---|---|
| Speeding 1 to 10 over, limit 65 or less | 0 | $20 to $30 |
| Speeding 1 to 5 over, limit above 65 | 0 | $20 to $25 |
| Texting while driving | Not on the schedule | $100 |
| Seat belt | Not on the schedule | $20 |
| Driving without a license | 0 | $150 |
| Overtime and double parking under city ordinance | 0 | Set by the city |

## How do I know a ticket isn't on the schedule?

The schedule is in NDCC 39-06.1-10, and NDDOT publishes it on its points page with this note: "For violations not listed, no points are assigned."

Following too closely, for example, doesn't appear on it.

## Do I still have to respond?

Yes. A ticket with no points is still a ticket. If you don't pay the fee, post bond or ask for a hearing, you're deemed to have admitted the violation. Failing to appear without paying or posting bond is a class B misdemeanor.

## Should I elect a course for a no-point ticket?

No. The election keeps points off, and there are none. You'd use up your one election for the next 12 months.

## Should I take a course anyway?

Only if you already have points. The 3-point reduction works on your existing total. If your record is clean, a course changes nothing on it.

| Violation | Points |
|---|---|
| Fleeing a peace officer | 24 |
| Leaving the scene, injury or death | 18 |
| Speeding 46 or more over | 15 |
| Leaving the scene, property damage | 14 |

posts.content:
## What does the law require?

It depends on the road (NDCC 39-10-26).

**On the interstate or a multilane highway outside a city.** When an emergency vehicle is parked or stopped with amber, blue, white or red lights flashing, you yield "by moving to a lane that is not adjacent" to it, if you can do that safely. If you can't, you slow down and keep a safe speed.

**At the scene of an emergency.** When an emergency vehicle is stopped there with its lights on, approaching traffic moves to the right edge and stops. After stopping, you can go past at your own risk when the road is clear.

## Does it cover snowplows and road crews?

It covers vehicles operated by or for NDDOT to maintain the state highway system, when they're stopped on the interstate or a multilane highway with amber or white lights flashing.

## What about an emergency vehicle coming up behind me?

Pull to the right edge of the road, clear of any intersection, and stop until it has passed.

## What is the penalty?

A $50 fee and 2 points. The points come from the schedule's entry for failing to yield the right of way.

## What if there's a crash?

Causing an accident with an emergency vehicle or a state maintenance vehicle that has its lights on is an infraction. It's 2 points, and it's one of the offenses in NDCC 39-06.1-05 that can't be resolved by paying a fee.

## Can I keep the points off?

For the ordinary $50 violation, yes. It's worth 2 points, so you can elect a driver training course at court when you post bond.

For the crash version, no. Offenses listed in section 39-06.1-05 are excluded from the election.

posts.title: North Dakota speed limits, and how they change your ticket
posts.seoTitle: North Dakota Speed Limits and Speeding Points
posts.description: North Dakota speed limits run from 20 near schools to 80 on the interstate. Above a 65 limit, a speeding ticket costs more and carries more points.
posts.answer: North Dakota's limits are 25 mph in business and residence districts, 55 on gravel and unposted county roads, 65 on posted two-lane highways, 70 on divided multilane highways and 80 on the interstate. Where the limit is posted above 65, speeding costs $5 per mph over and points start at 6 over.

faq.q: What is the speed limit on the interstate in North Dakota?
faq.a: 80 mph on access-controlled, paved and divided multilane interstate highways, unless otherwise posted or required by conditions.

faq.q: What is the speed limit on a gravel road in North Dakota?
faq.a: 55 mph on gravel, dirt or loose-surface highways, unless conditions require a lower speed.

faq.q: What is the speed limit in town in North Dakota?
faq.a: 25 mph in a business district, residence district or public park, unless a different speed is posted.

posts.content:
## What are North Dakota's speed limits?

From NDCC 39-09-02, unless a sign says otherwise:

| Where | Limit |
|---|---|
| Near a railroad crossing or intersection with an obstructed view | 20 mph |
| Passing a school during recess, or when children are arriving or leaving | 20 mph |
| Business district, residence district or public park | 25 mph |
| Gravel, dirt and loose-surface roads | 55 mph |
| Paved two-lane county and township roads with no limit posted | 55 mph |
| Paved two-lane highways, if posted | 65 mph |
| Paved and divided multilane highways | 70 mph |
| Access-controlled, divided, multilane interstate highways | 80 mph |

NDDOT and local authorities can post lower limits.

## Is the posted limit always legal to drive?

No. The basic rule comes first: you may not drive faster than is "reasonable and prudent under the conditions." On ice or in fog, the posted speed can get you a [careless driving ticket](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-careless-driving-ticket).

## Why does the posted limit matter for a ticket?

North Dakota has two speeding schedules. The line is a posted limit above 65.

| 10 mph over | Limit 65 or less | Limit above 65 |
|---|---|---|
| Points | 0 | 1 |
| Fee | $30 | $50 |

| 20 mph over | Limit 65 or less | Limit above 65 |
|---|---|---|
| Points | 3 | 5 |
| Fee | $80 | $120 |

So 90 in an 80 zone is 1 point and $50. 65 in a 55 zone is no points and $30.

## What about school zones and work zones?

They have their own fees. See [school zone and work zone speeding](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-school-zone-work-zone-speeding).

## What does the ticket have to say?

The speed you're alleged to have driven and the lawful speed at that place. NDCC 39-09-02 requires the complaint to specify both.

## Where are the full schedules?

[Speeding ticket points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-points) and [speeding ticket cost](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-speeding-ticket-cost).

A work zone ticket is $150 for 1 to 10 over, plus $2 for each mph above that, but only when workers are present and the sign says "Minimum Fee $150." Points follow the regular speeding schedule.

faq.q: How much is a school zone speeding ticket in North Dakota?
faq.a: $40 for 1 to 10 mph over the posted speed, plus $1 for each additional mph, unless the regular speeding fee would be greater.

faq.q: How much is a construction zone speeding ticket in North Dakota?

faq.q: Do work zone speeding tickets have more points in North Dakota?

posts.content:
## What is the school zone limit?

Twenty miles per hour "when passing a school during school recess or while children are going to or leaving school during opening or closing hours," unless local authorities post a lower speed.

## What does a school zone ticket cost?

| Over the posted speed | Fee |
|---|---|
| 1 to 10 mph | $40 |
| 15 mph | $45 |
| 20 mph | $50 |

The law says the regular speeding fee applies if it would be greater. At 20 over, the regular fee is $80, so that's what you'd owe.

## What does a work zone ticket cost?

| Over the posted speed | Fee |
|---|---|
| 1 to 10 mph | $150 |
| 15 mph | $160 |
| 20 mph | $170 |
| 25 mph | $180 |

## When does the work zone fee apply?

Only when two things are true: people engaged in construction are present at the time and place, and the posted speed limit sign states "Minimum Fee $150." If either is missing, the regular speeding fee applies.

## How many points?

The same as any speeding ticket at that speed. Where the limit is 65 or less, 1 to 10 over is 0 points, 11 to 15 is 1, 16 to 20 is 3, and 21 to 25 is 5.

## Can a city charge more?

City ordinances can set their own amounts. The Fargo Municipal Court, for example, lists $80 for 1 to 10 over in school and construction zones, plus $2 for each mph above that. Your citation shows what you owe.

## Can I keep the points off?

Yes, if the ticket is worth 5 points or fewer. Elect a driver training course at court when you post bond. The fee doesn't change.

## What if the ticket is for 0 points?

Pay it. There's nothing for a course to keep off.

faq.a: Three points, with a $50 fee.

faq.q: How many points is drag racing in North Dakota?
faq.a: Ten points, with a $100 fee.

posts.content:
## What is exhibition driving?

NDCC 39-08-03.1 defines it as driving "in a manner which disturbs the peace by creating or causing unnecessary engine noise, tire squeal, skid, or slide upon acceleration or braking," or making "unnecessarily abrupt turns."

## What counts as racing?

- **Drag race:** two or more vehicles starting side by side and accelerating to outdistance each other, or vehicles timed over the same course.
- **Race:** trying to outgain or outdistance another vehicle, or keeping another vehicle from passing.

## Where does it apply?

On a "highway, street, alley, sidewalk, or any public or private parking lot or area." A store parking lot counts.

Organized events on a track or private area set aside for racing are not covered.

## What are the penalties?

| Violation | Fee | Points |
|---|---|---|
| Exhibition driving | $50 | 3 |
| Drag racing or racing | $100 | 10 |

## How close is 10 points to a suspension?

Two points. A stop sign ticket or a speeding ticket for 16 over would do it. For a driver under 18, 10 points is past the 6 that cancels a license.

## Can a course keep the points off?

For exhibition driving, yes. It's 3 points, so you can elect a driver training course at court when you post bond.

For racing, no. It's 10 points, and the election stops at 5.

## What can a course do after a racing ticket?

Take 3 points off, from 10 to 7. Do it soon. At 10, one small ticket suspends you. At 7, you have room.

Send the certificate to drs@nd.gov. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

posts.title: Out-of-state tickets and North Dakota points
posts.seoTitle: Out-of-State Tickets and North Dakota Points
posts.description: North Dakota doesn't add points for most tickets its drivers get in other states. Visitors ticketed in North Dakota answer to their home state.
posts.answer: If you hold a North Dakota license and get an ordinary ticket in another state, North Dakota doesn't add points for it. Points are added only for serious criminal offenses such as DUI or reckless driving. If you're from another state and get a ticket in North Dakota, NDDOT can report it to your home state, which decides what happens.

faq.q: Do out-of-state tickets put points on a North Dakota license?
faq.a: Not for ordinary violations. NDCC 39-06-27 allows points only for a conviction of a criminal offense equivalent to those listed in section 39-06.1-05, such as DUI or reckless driving.

faq.q: Does North Dakota report tickets to other states?
faq.a: It can. Under NDCC 39-06-26 the director may notify the licensing authority in the nonresident driver's home state.

faq.q: I live in another state and got a North Dakota ticket. Will I get points?
faq.a: That is decided by your home state. Contact the licensing agency of the state where you are licensed.

posts.content:
## I have a North Dakota license and got a ticket in another state. Do I get points?

Usually not. NDCC 39-06-27 says the section "may not be construed as authorizing the assessment of points against a resident's driving record" except on conviction of a criminal offense "equivalent to one of those offenses defined in section 39-06.1-05."

Those offenses include driving under the influence, reckless driving, leaving the scene of an accident, and driving while suspended.

## Can North Dakota still act on an out-of-state conviction?

Yes. The director may suspend or revoke a resident's license on notice of a conviction in another state or a tribal court for an offense that would be grounds for suspension or revocation here.

## Do I still have to deal with the ticket?

Yes, with the court in the state that issued it. Ignoring it can cost you your driving privilege in that state.

## I'm from another state and got a ticket in North Dakota. What happens?

You respond to the North Dakota court on your citation within the time it gives. NDDOT "may notify the licensing authority in the state in which the nonresident resides or is licensed."

What your home state does with it depends on that state's rules. The Fargo Municipal Court gives the same advice on points: contact the state you're licensed by.

## Can a visitor use the North Dakota course?

The course affects a North Dakota driving record. If your license is from another state, ask your home state's licensing agency what it accepts before you pay for any course. We'd rather not sell you one that doesn't help.

## How do I see what North Dakota has on my record?

Order a [North Dakota driving record](/north-dakota/blog/check-points-north-dakota-driving-record) for $3. It shows your point total.

## What about tickets on a reservation?

The director can act on reports from tribal courts. The same limit on points applies: they're added only for the serious criminal offenses.

posts.content:
## What is a temporary restricted license?

NDDOT describes it as "a restricted license issued to persons whose driving privileges have been suspended or revoked for certain offenses." It authorizes driving a non-commercial vehicle for work, for education, or for essential life maintenance needs.

It limits you to specific days and times.

## Who can't get one?

- Anyone under 18
- Anyone who wants it to operate a commercial motor vehicle

## Can I get one on the first day of my suspension?

No. NDDOT says that by law the driver "must serve a portion of the suspension with no type of restricted driving privileges," and the length depends on the reason for the suspension.

A points suspension at 12 points is 7 days. Ask NDDOT whether applying makes sense for a suspension that short.

## How do I apply?

Fill out the TRL application, form SFN 2254, and submit it to NDDOT's Driver License Division. The phone number is 701-328-2604, answered Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 9 to 3.

## What if I drive outside the restrictions?

Violating the restrictions on a restricted license is on the point schedule. It's 4 points for a restricted certificate or license, and 3 points for a corrective lens restriction.

## What do I need to be fully reinstated?

Serve the suspension and pay the reinstatement fee, which is $50 for a points suspension. NDDOT's online system lists your outstanding requirements.

## How do I avoid needing one?

Keep your total under 12. A defensive driving course takes 3 points off once every 12 months, and it works best before you reach 12. [Suspended for points](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-license-suspended-for-points) explains what happens at each total.

posts.content:
## What are the steps?

From the North Dakota Court System's payment guide:

1. Go to publicsearch.ndcourts.gov.
2. Select State of North Dakota under Case Records, then click Criminal/Traffic.
3. Enter the defendant's last and first name and click Search. Or choose Citation and enter the citation number.
4. Click the blue case number for the ticket you want to pay.
5. Click Make Payment, in the upper or lower right corner.
6. On the checkout page, confirm the amount and click Checkout.
7. Enter the cardholder information and process the payment.
8. Print the receipt.

## My citation number isn't working. Why?

It may need leading zeros. The court system says the number "may need to be padded with extra zeros to reach the required length of 10 digits," for example 0000987654.

## My ticket isn't there. What now?

Wait. The courts ask you to allow 4 days from the date of the citation for processing. If it still doesn't appear, call the clerk of court in the city or county where the ticket was issued.

## There's no Make Payment button. Why?

The case may not be eligible for online payment. Criminal traffic offenses, for example, require a court appearance. Contact the clerk.

## Which cards are accepted?

Visa, Mastercard and Discover. American Express is not accepted.

## Do city tickets work the same way?

Several city courts use the same site. Bismarck's court tells drivers to choose a location under Payment and pick Bismarck in the municipal section. Fargo's court also sends drivers to the state's public search site. Williston and West Fargo have their own payment links.

## How long do I have?

If you post bond by mail for a state-law ticket, 14 days from the date of the citation. City courts give the same 14 days.

## Want the course instead of points? Don't pay online

Don't pay online first. The state courts' payment site says "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT" if you want to take a defensive driving course instead of points. The election is made in writing to the clerk of court when you post bond, in person or by mail in the same envelope as the citation, within 14 days of the citation (ND Legal Self Help Center guide, rev. July 2024). There is no online way to elect it.

## What should I do before I pay?

Decide about points. Paying admits the violation. If the ticket is worth 1 to 5 points and you want them kept off, you have to tell the court you elect a driver training course at the time you post bond. Call the clerk first and ask how to record that. [Should you just pay?](/north-dakota/blog/should-i-pay-my-north-dakota-ticket)

posts.description: To contest a North Dakota ticket, request a hearing and post a bond equal to the fee within 14 days. What happens at the hearing and on appeal.
posts.answer: Sign the request for hearing on your citation and post a bond equal to the fee within 14 days. At the hearing, the state or city has to prove the violation by a preponderance of the evidence. If the prosecution doesn't show up or isn't ready, the charge is dismissed. posts.content:
## How do I ask for a hearing?

Date and sign the request for hearing on your copy of the citation, return it to the court, and post the bond. The bond equals the statutory fee for the violation. You have 14 days from the citation.

## When is the hearing?

At the time on the citation, at a time set in response to your request, or at a later date set at your first appearance, no more than 90 days out.

## What does the prosecution have to prove?

That you committed the violation, "by a preponderance of the evidence." That means more likely than not. It's a lower standard than in a criminal case.

## What if the officer or prosecutor doesn't come?

If you appear at the scheduled time and "the prosecution does not appear or is not ready to prove the commission of a charged violation," the official has to dismiss the charge.

## What happens if I win?

The bond is returned. City courts ask you to bring the receipt or mail you a check.

## What happens if I lose?

The bond is applied to the fee, and the court reports the violation to NDDOT within 10 days. NDDOT then enters the points.

## Can I appeal?

From a municipal court, yes. You can appeal to the district court for a new trial, with no filing fee. Notice of appeal has to be given within 30 days, in writing unless you give it orally at the time of the finding. There's no further appeal after that.

From a district judge or magistrate, no.

## Does an appeal stop the points?

No. The appeal doesn't stay the report to NDDOT. The district court can order a stay of up to 120 days if you apply for one with a certified copy of your driving record.

## Can I elect a course and contest the ticket?

The election is made when you post bond, and the bond is forfeited when you elect. If your goal is to keep points off a ticket worth 5 points or fewer, the election is the surer route. Ask the clerk how your court handles it. [How to elect a course](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## Will a traffic finding be used against me elsewhere?

The law says an admission or finding of a traffic violation is not admissible as evidence in any court, except in a proceeding involving your driver license.

## Where is the Fargo Municipal Court?

At 207 4th St. N., Fargo, ND 58102, on the second floor of the Fargo Civic Center. The office is open Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except legal holidays. The phone number is 701.241.1316 and the mailing address is PO Box 49, Fargo, ND 58107.

## How do I pay a Fargo traffic ticket?

- **Online.** The court says payments for noncriminal offenses "may be made online at the North Dakota Supreme Court Public Search website."
- **By phone.** Call the clerk's office at 701.241.1316 with a bank or credit card.
- **In person or by mail.** Cash, checks, money orders, Visa, Mastercard and Discover are accepted.

## How long do I have?

Fourteen days. The court's instructions say the bond or fee must be paid "no later than 14 days after you received this citation." If you choose neither option on the citation, you're deemed to have admitted the violation, and your license may be suspended.

## How do I contest the ticket?

Date and sign the request for hearing on your copy of the citation, return it to the court, and post the bond, all within 14 days. The court will notify you of the hearing date. A finding against you can be appealed to the district court.

## What if my ticket isn't from Fargo police?

Tickets written in Cass County outside the city court's jurisdiction go to the Cass County Clerk of District Court, 211 S. 9th St., Fargo, 701.451.6900. For a ticket from somewhere else, the court's contact information is on the front of the citation.

## Does the court decide my points?

No. NDDOT does. The court reports the violation to NDDOT, and NDDOT enters the points from the state schedule. A stop sign ticket is 2 points. Speeding is 0 to 15 depending on your speed. [Points by violation](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-by-violation).

## How do I keep the points off?

State law lets you elect a driver training course in lieu of points for a violation worth 5 points or fewer. You have to tell the court at the time you post bond, then get your certificate to NDDOT within 30 days.

Don't pay online first. The state courts' payment site says "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT" if you want to take a defensive driving course instead of points. The election is made in writing to the clerk of court when you post bond, in person or by mail in the same envelope as the citation, within 14 days of the citation (ND Legal Self Help Center guide, rev. July 2024). There is no online way to elect it.

Fargo's court pages don't explain how to record that election. Call the clerk at 701.241.1316 before you pay and ask.

[How the election works](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## What if I've already paid?

The points will post. A defensive driving course takes 3 off, once every 12 months. Email the certificate to drs@nd.gov. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).

## Where is the Bismarck Municipal Court?

At 514 E. Thayer Ave., Bismarck, ND 58501. The window is open Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The phone number is 701-355-1350.

## How do I pay a Bismarck traffic ticket?

- **Online.** Go to NDCourts.gov, open the search and pay fines page, choose a location under Payment, and pick Bismarck in the municipal section. Search by the citation number on the top right of the ticket, or by name. The court says only computers and laptops work for online payment.
- **In person.** At the court window on Thayer Avenue.

Parking tickets use a different payment portal.

## How long do I have?

Fourteen calendar days. The court says your citation "MUST be paid within 14 calendar days" or you must appear on the date on the citation. Signing the citation when you receive it is not an admission of guilt.

## How do I contest the ticket?

Appear in court on the date on your citation, or on a Monday or Wednesday at 8 a.m. or 9 a.m. within 14 days. Sign and date the citation and pay the bond in full by check, cash or money order. If you're found not guilty, the bond is returned. Bring your receipt. A guilty finding can be appealed in writing within 30 days.

## What if my ticket isn't from Bismarck police?

A ticket from the Highway Patrol or the county sheriff goes to the district court, not the city court. The court named on your citation is the one to contact.

## Does the court decide my points?

No. NDDOT does. The court reports the violation to NDDOT, and NDDOT enters the points from the state schedule. A stop sign ticket is 2 points. Speeding is 0 to 15 depending on your speed. [Points by violation](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-points-by-violation).

## How do I keep the points off?

State law lets you elect a driver training course in lieu of points for a violation worth 5 points or fewer. You have to tell the court at the time you post bond, then get your certificate to NDDOT within 30 days.

Don't pay online first. The state courts' payment site says "STOP! DO NOT MAKE A PAYMENT" if you want to take a defensive driving course instead of points. The election is made in writing to the clerk of court when you post bond, in person or by mail in the same envelope as the citation, within 14 days of the citation (ND Legal Self Help Center guide, rev. July 2024). There is no online way to elect it.

The Bismarck court says it "has no authority regarding drivers' licenses or points," and its pages don't explain how to record an election. Call 701-355-1350 before you pay and ask.

[How the election works](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## What if I've already paid?

The points will post. A defensive driving course takes 3 off, once every 12 months. Email the certificate to drs@nd.gov. [How the course works](/north-dakota/blog/north-dakota-defensive-driving-course-points).
